This vignette describes how to add a model of aquatic mosquito ecology to
[`ramp.library`](https://github.com/dd-harp/ramp.library). Read the
[`ramp.xds` L interface vignette](https://dd-harp.github.io/ramp.xds/articles/L-interface.html)
first for an overview of how L modules connect to egg laying and emergence.
Before adding a module, check whether the model is already available in the
SimBA library.

An L module describes aquatic mosquito states in larval habitats. Its
methods operate on the habitat dimension, `nHabitats`, and use `s` as the
vector-species index. The habitat-to-patch `membership` vector is provided
when the module is set up.

## Creating a module template

The code chunks below can be extracted to create a starting R file. From
the directory containing this vignette, run:

```{r, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
knitr::purl(
  "L-How_To_Add_Model.Rmd",
  output = "Lmodule-newLname.R",
  documentation = 0,
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

The resulting file contains code examples that must be adapted before the
module is used. Replace `newLname` with a short, model-specific name. When
rendered, the chunks define the example functions but do not call them.

## General conventions

- Implement model methods as S3 methods named with the module class, such
  as `dLdt.newLname`.
- Use `s` to access the module at `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`.
- Store state indices in `xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix`, with one index per
  habitat for each habitat-level state.
- Keep state variables, derivatives, and discrete updates in the same
  order.
- Document model equations, states, parameters, inputs, outputs, and
  references with roxygen.
- Add tests for the module's equations, dimensions, and setup behavior.

## Module dynamics

Implement `dLdt.newLname` for a continuous-time model, or
`Update_Lt.newLname` for a discrete-time model. Both receive time `t`, the
dependent-variable vector `y`, the **`xds`** model object, and the species
index `s`. A continuous-time method returns derivatives; a discrete-time
method returns updated states. They are alternative solver interfaces, not
interchangeable equations.

The habitat-level egg input is available as
`xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]`. Extract the module states with `get_L_vars` and
use the indices and parameter values stored on the module object.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute derivatives for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::dLdt] for `newLname`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::dLdt
#' @return a numeric vector of derivatives, in state-variable order
#' @export
dLdt.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  eta <- xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]

  with(ramp.xds::get_L_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
      # Replace this expression with the model's derivative equation.
      dL <- rep(0, xds_obj$nHabitats)
      derivatives <- c(dL)
      return(derivatives)
    })
  })
}
```

If the model has multiple states, extract each state in
`get_L_vars.newLname`, compute each derivative here, and concatenate them in
the same order used by `setup_L_ix.newLname`.

The discrete-time method has the same arguments and returns updated states
in that order. Write the model's discrete update equations directly; do not
substitute the continuous-time derivative or an Euler step unless that is
the model being implemented.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Update states for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::Update_Lt] for `newLname`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::Update_Lt
#' @return a numeric vector of updated states, in state-variable order
#' @export
Update_Lt.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  eta <- xds_obj$terms$eta[[s]]

  with(ramp.xds::get_L_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
      # Replace this expression with the model's discrete update.
      Lt <- rep(0, xds_obj$nHabitats)
      states <- c(Lt)
      return(states)
    })
  })
}
```

## Bionomics and effect sizes

`LBionomics.newLname` updates baseline parameter values at time `t` and
resets effect sizes. `LEffectSizes.newLname` applies the configured effect
sizes to those baseline values. Implement these methods for parameters that
use time-varying forcing or vector-control effects; use the existing
bionomics forcing functions where they match the parameter.

For each affected parameter `p1`, store its baseline as `p1_t`, its effect
size as `es_p1`, and its effective value as `p1`. The example assumes
`p1_t` and `p2_t` have already been initialized on the module object.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Mosquito bionomics for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Update baseline parameters and reset effect sizes.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::LBionomics
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
LBionomics.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
    # Replace these assignments with the appropriate forcing functions.
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p1_t <- p1
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p2_t <- p2
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$es_p1 <- rep(1, xds_obj$nHabitats)
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$es_p2 <- rep(1, xds_obj$nHabitats)
    return(xds_obj)
  })
}

#' @title Apply effect sizes for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Apply vector-control effect sizes to baseline parameters.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::LEffectSizes
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
LEffectSizes.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p1 <- p1_t * es_p1
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p2 <- p2_t * es_p2
    return(xds_obj)
  })
}
```

## Module object and setup

`make_L_obj_newLname` creates the module object and initializes its
parameters. `setup_L_obj.newLname` attaches the object at
`xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]`, sets up initial values, and configures habitat search
weights using the supplied `membership` vector.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Make the `newLname` module object
#' @param nHabitats the number of habitats in the model
#' @param options a named list of parameter values
#' @return an L module object
#' @export
make_L_obj_newLname <- function(nHabitats, options = list(), p1 = 1, p2 = 1) {
  with(options, {
    L_obj <- list(
      p1 = ramp.xds::checkIt(p1, nHabitats),
      p2 = ramp.xds::checkIt(p2, nHabitats),
      p1_t = ramp.xds::checkIt(p1, nHabitats),
      p2_t = ramp.xds::checkIt(p2, nHabitats),
      es_p1 = rep(1, nHabitats),
      es_p2 = rep(1, nHabitats),
      nHabitats = nHabitats
    )
    class(L_obj) <- "newLname"
    return(L_obj)
  })
}

#' @title Set up `newLname` (**L**)
#' @description Implements [ramp.xds::setup_L_obj] for `newLname`.
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_L_obj
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_L_obj.newLname <- function(Lname, membership, xds_obj,
                                 options = list(), s = 1) {
  L_obj <- make_L_obj_newLname(xds_obj$nHabitats, options)
  class(L_obj) <- c("newLname", paste0("newLname_", xds_obj$xds))
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]] <- L_obj
  xds_obj <- ramp.xds::setup_L_inits(xds_obj, options = options, s = s)
  xds_obj <- ramp.xds::setup_habitat_search_weights(
    "setup", xds_obj, list(membership = membership), s = s
  )
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

## Parameters

Implement `get_L_pars.newLname` to return the module parameters as a named
list, and `change_L_pars.newLname` to update the parameters named in
`options` while leaving other parameters unchanged. Check supplied values
against `xds_obj$nHabitats`; parameter vectors should match the habitat
dimension.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Get parameters for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_L_pars
#' @return a named list of parameters
#' @export
get_L_pars.newLname <- function(xds_obj, s = 1) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
    return(list(p1 = p1, p2 = p2))
  })
}

#' @title Change parameters for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_L_pars
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_L_pars.newLname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  nHabitats <- xds_obj$nHabitats
  if ("p1" %in% names(options)) {
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p1_t <- ramp.xds::checkIt(options$p1, nHabitats)
  }
  if ("p2" %in% names(options)) {
    xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$p2_t <- ramp.xds::checkIt(options$p2, nHabitats)
  }
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

## State indices and extraction

`setup_L_ix.newLname` assigns a contiguous range of indices to each state.
Allocate one index per habitat for each habitat-level state, and update
`max_ix` after each range. `get_L_vars.newLname` extracts named states from
the dependent-variable vector `y`.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Set up state indices for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_L_ix
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @importFrom utils tail
#' @export
setup_L_ix.newLname <- function(xds_obj, s) {
  L_ix <- seq(from = xds_obj$max_ix + 1, length.out = xds_obj$nHabitats)
  xds_obj$max_ix <- utils::tail(L_ix, 1)
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix <- list(L_ix = L_ix)
  return(xds_obj)
}

#' @title Extract states for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::get_L_vars
#' @return a named list of state variables
#' @export
get_L_vars.newLname <- function(y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix, {
    L <- y[L_ix]
    return(list(L = L))
  })
}
```

If the module has more than one state variable, create an index range for
each one and include each named state in the returned list.

## Initial values

`make_L_inits_newLname` returns defaults as a named list with one value per
habitat for each state. `setup_L_inits.newLname` stores the list on the
module object; users can inspect it with `get_L_inits` and update it with
`change_L_inits.newLname`.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Make initial values for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @param nHabitats the number of habitats in the model
#' @param options a named list of initial values
#' @param L the initial value for state `L`
#' @return a named list of initial values
#' @export
make_L_inits_newLname <- function(nHabitats, options = list(), L = 1) {
  with(options, {
    L <- ramp.xds::checkIt(L, nHabitats)
    return(list(L = L))
  })
}

#' @title Set up initial values for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::setup_L_inits
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
setup_L_inits.newLname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits <- make_L_inits_newLname(
    xds_obj$nHabitats, options
  )
  return(xds_obj)
}

#' @title Change initial values for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::change_L_inits
#' @return an **`xds`** model object
#' @export
change_L_inits.newLname <- function(xds_obj, options = list(), s = 1) {
  with(options, {
    if (!is.null(L)) {
      xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$inits$L <- ramp.xds::checkIt(
        L, xds_obj$nHabitats
      )
    }
  })
  return(xds_obj)
}
```

## Emergence

`F_emerge.newLname` returns a habitat-level vector of adult emergence,
usually a rate for a continuous-time model or a number for a discrete-time
model. The shared emergence interface aggregates these values to patches
using habitat membership.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Compute emergence for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::F_emerge
#' @return a numeric vector of length `nHabitats`
#' @export
F_emerge.newLname <- function(t, y, xds_obj, s) {
  with(ramp.xds::get_L_vars(y, xds_obj, s), {
    with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]], {
      # Replace this expression with the model's emergence equation.
      alpha <- rep(0, xds_obj$nHabitats)
      return(alpha)
    })
  })
}
```

## Parsing outputs and optional methods

`parse_L_orbits.newLname` extracts each state from the solver output
matrix, using the indices stored on the module object, and returns a named
list. Add derived quantities only when they are useful model outputs.

```{r, eval=TRUE, purl=TRUE}
#' @title Parse outputs for `newLname` (**L**)
#' @inheritParams ramp.xds::parse_L_orbits
#' @return a named list of state-variable orbits
#' @export
parse_L_orbits.newLname <- function(outputs, xds_obj, s) {
  with(xds_obj$L_obj[[s]]$ix, {
    L <- outputs[, L_ix]
    return(list(L = L))
  })
}
```

`steady_state_L.newLname` is optional and applies to continuous-time models
when a steady-state solution is available. It receives habitat-level egg
input `eta` and returns a named list of steady-state values. The shared
`get_L_orbits`, `xds_plot_L`, and `xds_lines_L` functions provide access
to and visualization of parsed model output; a module-specific plotting
method is not required.

## The `basicL` reference model

The `basicL` module in `ramp.xds` is an example of a habitat-level model.
It tracks larval density \(L\) and implements

\[
\frac{dL}{dt}
= \eta - \left(\psi e^{-\xi L} + \phi + \theta L\right)L,
\qquad
\alpha = \psi e^{-\xi L}L.
\]

Its states and parameters each have one value per habitat. Consult
`aquatic-L-basicL.R` in the `ramp.xds` source for a complete implementation
of its setup, parameter, dynamics, initial-value, emergence, and output
methods.
